verdicts.title: Karchmer-Wigderson Games for Hazard-free Computation
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We present a Karchmer-Wigderson game to study the complexity of hazard-free formulas. This new game is both a generalization of the monotone Karchmer-Wigderson game and an analog of the classical Boolean Karchmer-Wigderson game. Therefore, it acts as a bridge between the existing monotone and general games.

verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract introduces a Karchmer-Wigderson game for hazard-free formulas and proves size/depth bounds for specific functions like the multiplexer; it does not address asymptotic dimension, coarse geometry, or the KRW direct-sum/composition conjecture.

verdicts.title: Multiparty Karchmer-Wigderson Games and Threshold Circuits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We suggest a generalization of Karchmer-Wigderson communication games to the multiparty setting. Our generalization turns out to be tightly connected to circuits consisting of threshold gates. This allows us to obtain new explicit constructions of such circuits for several functions. In particular, we provide an explicit (polynomial-time computable) log-depth monotone formula for Majority function, consisting only of 3-bit majority gates and variables. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a multiparty generalization of KW games connected to threshold circuits and an explicit log-depth majority formula, with no mention of asymptotic dimension, coarse geometry, or the KRW direct-sum / block-composition lower bound.

verdicts.title: Asymptotic Properties of Hilbert Geometry

verdicts.title: One-way communication complexity and the Neciporuk lower bound on formula size
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper the Neciporuk method for proving lower bounds on the size of Boolean formulae is reformulated in terms of one-way communication complexity. We investigate the scenarios of probabilistic formulae, nondeterministic formulae, and quantum formulae. verdicts.title: Oriented Ramsey numbers of graded digraphs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We show that any graded digraph $D$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $Δ$ has an oriented Ramsey number of at most $C^Δn$ for some absolute constant $C > 1$, improving upon a recent result of Fox, He, and Wigderson. verdicts.title: Polynomials vanishing on Cartesian products: The Elekes-Szabó Theorem revisited
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Let $F\in\mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ be a constant-degree polynomial,and let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb C$ be finite sets of size $n$.
